concept.body: Exterior angle = the turn between one side extended and the next side. Walking the whole boundary returns you to your starting heading, so the exterior angles of every polygon sum to 360° — no formula, no dependence on n. At each vertex, interior + exterior = 180° because they share a straight line.

explanationVariants: Three exterior angles of a triangle total 360: the third is 140°.

widget.prompt: Two exterior angles of a triangle are 90° and 130°. The third?

commonErrors.feedback: 320 treats the total as 540 — that's a pentagon's INTERIOR sum. Exterior lap: 360 − 220 = 140°.
220 is the two turns so far. Complete the lap: 360 − 220 = 140°.

steps.body: Walk the boundary of any polygon. At each vertex you TURN through the **exterior angle** — the angle between one side extended and the next side. Finish the lap and you're facing your starting direction again: one complete rotation. So the exterior angles of ANY polygon — 3 sides or 300, regular or lopsided — sum to exactly **360°**.

explanationVariants: One full lap = one full turn = 360°, regardless of the number of sides.
The walker ends facing the way they started; the turns total a single rotation: 360°.

widget.prompt: Exterior angles of a 23-gon (one at each vertex): what do they sum to?

commonErrors.feedback: 3780 = (23 − 2) × 180 is the INTERIOR sum. Exterior angles always close one lap: 360°.
4140 = 23 × 180 pairs every interior with its exterior — the exteriors ALONE make one turn: 360°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Every polygon's exterior angles sum to 360°.

steps.body: At each vertex the interior and exterior angles sit on a straight line, so they're **supplementary**: interior + exterior = 180°. An interior of 108° leaves an exterior of 72°. This little exchange rate lets you hop between the two worlds at will.

explanationVariants: Exterior = 180 − 108 = 72° — the two share a straight line at the vertex.

widget.prompt: A vertex has interior angle 108°. Its exterior angle?

commonErrors.feedback: 252 = 360 − 108 subtracts from the wrong total — the pair shares a straight LINE (180°), not a full turn: 72°.
54 = 108 ÷ 2 halves the interior — there's no halving here. Supplement: 180 − 108 = 72°.

widget.prompt: Why do a polygon's exterior angles always total 360°, no matter its shape?

options.label: Walking the boundary returns you to your starting direction — the turns make exactly one full rotation
options.feedback: The turns are the exterior angles, and closing the loop means facing the original heading: 360° in total.

options.label: Because each exterior angle equals 360 divided by the number of sides
options.feedback: That's only true for REGULAR polygons. Irregular ones share the turns unevenly — yet still complete one lap: 360°.

options.label: Because interior angles also sum to 360°
options.feedback: Interior sums GROW with n — (n − 2) × 180. It's the exteriors that stay pinned at one rotation.

options.label: It's a rule with occasional exceptions for concave shapes
options.feedback: For convex polygons the lap argument holds without exception — the sum is exactly 360°. (Concave shapes need signed turns — beyond this course.)

explanationVariants: The five turns must complete one lap: what's missing from 360 is 70°.

widget.prompt: Four exterior angles of a pentagon are 85°, 60°, 70°, and 75°. The fifth?

commonErrors.feedback: 250 = 540 − 290 reaches for the INTERIOR sum. Exterior angles close a 360° lap: 360 − 290 = 70°.
290 is the four turns so far — the fifth finishes the lap: 360 − 290 = 70°.

widget.prompt: You need the interior angle sum of a 50-gon and also one exterior angle question. Which fact requires NO formula at all?

options.label: The exterior sum — it's 360° for every polygon
options.feedback: The lap argument is size-blind: 3 sides or 50, the turns total one rotation.

options.label: The interior sum — it's always 180°
options.feedback: 180° is the TRIANGLE's interior sum only; a 50-gon holds (50 − 2) × 180 = 8640°. The formula-free one is the exterior 360°.

options.label: Both need the (n − 2) formula
options.feedback: Only the interior sum does. Exteriors ignore n entirely: one lap, 360°.

options.label: Neither — both depend on side length
options.feedback: Angle sums never see side LENGTHS at all — and the exterior sum doesn't even see the side COUNT: 360°.

hints: In a regular polygon all exterior angles are equal, and together they make 360°.
explanationVariants: Equal turns summing to 360: n = 360/24 = 15 sides.
Fifteen turns of 24° complete the lap: 15 × 24 = 360. ✓

widget.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 24°. How many sides?

commonErrors.feedback: 7.5 = 180 ÷ 24 divides into a straight line — the turns fill a full LAP: 360 ÷ 24 = 15. (And a polygon can't have half a side.)
336 = 360 − 24 subtracts instead of counting turns. Each turn is 24° of the 360° lap: 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides.

takeaways: Exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360° — walking the boundary is one full turn.
At each vertex, interior + exterior = 180° (straight line).
Regular polygon: n × (each exterior) = 360, so n = 360 ÷ exterior.
